# Check If Two String Arrays are Equivalent.

@example Both arrays glue together to "pineapple", cut in different places.
["pin","e","apple"]
["pine","app","le"]
=> true

@example The same two strings in the other order give "sunday" and "daysun".
["sun","day"]
["day","sun"]
=> false

@example "overla" is one letter short of "overlap".
["over","lap"]
["overla"]
=> false

# One string on each side, the same.
["x"]
["x"]
=> true

# The same letters, two of each, in another order: "abba" and "aabb".
["ab","ba"]
["aabb"]
=> false

# word1's text is a prefix of word2's.
["go"]
["go","od"]
=> false

# word2's text is a prefix of word1's.
["tea","m"]
["te","a"]
=> false

# Equal lengths; only the first letter differs.
["bxyz"]
["c","xyz"]
=> false

# Equal lengths; only the last letter differs.
["mo","on"]
["m","oo","m"]
=> false

# The first difference is where a string of word1 begins: "abcd" and
# "abdd".
["ab","cd"]
["abd","d"]
=> false

# One letter per string against a single string.
["r","a","d","a","r"]
["radar"]
=> true

# Identical arrays.
["q","rs","tuv"]
["q","rs","tuv"]
=> true

# The largest arrays: 1000 strings of one letter, and one string of 1000

# 1000 letters on each side, differing only in the last one (index 999).
["",""]
["","","m"]
=> false

# A text of 3 letters against one of 1000 that starts with it.
["abc"]
[""]
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
["bbabbbb"]
["bb","ababb"]
=> false

@gen 2 small
["baaaa"]
["a","aaa","a"]
=> false

@gen 3 small
["a","a","b"]
["a","ab"]
=> true

@gen 4 small
["aab"]
["aab"]
=> true

@gen 5 small
["ab"]
["a","b"]
=> true

@gen 6 small
["b"]
["ba"]
=> false

@gen 7 small
["baaaaab"]
["babaaab"]
=> false

@gen 8 small
["a","b","a","b"]
["bbab"]
=> false
